approach:
Root cause, read in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs:373-419. `failure_section` is the one place a failed check's output is chosen for storage. It cuts cleanup only at a header line (`is_cleanup_line`, 345: "Post job cleanup", "Post Run ", "Cleaning up orphan processes"), and only at or after the last runner marker or `##[error]` line. When no header is matched, it keeps a plain tail. When the header is the last line of the block, the git credential-removal lines above it stay. Nothing tells a reader that no failing test section was found. Fix: change only `checks.rs` for recognition, and give the storing stage the missing knowledge. (1) `is_cleanup_line` recognises the content of the cleanup block as well as its header. (2) After the existing header cut, a new `cleanup_start` walks BACK from the end and strips the trailing cleanup block. It stops at a `##[group]Run ` step start, at the anchor, or after more than 1 consecutive unrecognised line. Setup and checkout git lines at the start of a log therefore cannot be mistaken for the block. (3) `failure_section` returns `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE` only when the input had a non-blank line and cleanup removed all of it. Empty output stays empty. (4) `detail_from_job_logs` (gh/client.rs:296) appends ONE note as the LAST line of the whole tail when any readable shard log has no runner marker. The note names those shards. Its line and byte cost is reserved inside the 200-line and 64 KiB limits. The last line is the one every later reader keeps: `with_failure_detail` (every branch of `failure_section` keeps the end, checks.rs:394-418), `CheckFailure::of` (last 3000 bytes) and the verifier brief (last 60 lines, briefs.rs:1114-1127). `with_failure_detail`, the local run (checks.rs:618) and `CheckFailure::of` (send_back.rs:297) all go through `failure_section`, so every producer of a failed record is covered. No record shape, admission or gate code changes.

How the previous round's findings are answered:
- Finding 1: the note moves from first to last, is counted inside the limit, and an end-to-end test checks it after storage, in the send-back and in the verifier brief.
- Finding 2: the forward density rule is replaced by a backward walk with a step-start boundary. `##[group]` and `##[endgroup]` are no longer treated as cleanup.
- Finding 3: the empty-output note is gated on a non-blank input.
- Finding 4: briefs.rs is added to the dependents with a test.
- Finding 5: the CHANGELOG states what the code did. Both log shapes (with and without `##[error]`) are tested.
- Finding 6: the doc comment is rewritten and the header predicate is split out.

decisions.choice: Put the 'no failing test section' note at the END of the whole stored tail, once, naming the shards without a runner marker, and count it inside the limits. In `detail_from_job_logs`, find the shards with no marker first, build the note, then reserve its 1 line and its byte length (plus 1 line when a `failing units:` line will be added) before computing `per_lines` and `per_bytes` (client.rs:334-339). `checks.rs` supplies `has_failing_section(text)`, `no_test_section_note(&[&str])` and the constants `NO_TEST_SECTION_PREFIX` and `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE`.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. Every tail-based reader keeps the last line: `failure_section`'s branches keep the end (checks.rs:394-395 whole; 402-403 and 405-406 `tail_lines`; 417 the last 20 lines of the jump case). `CheckFailure::of` keeps the last 3000 bytes (send_back.rs:297). The verifier brief keeps the last 60 lines / 6 KiB (briefs.rs:1114-1127), after `check_result_view` strips only a LEADING units line (verify.rs:77-85). With the reserve, one shard totals at most 199 lines plus the note, so `with_failure_detail`'s 199/200-line re-cut (checks.rs:440-446) drops nothing. A multi-shard note is built once, so earlier shards' notes cannot be pushed out by a later shard's long section. An existing assertion breaks and is updated: gh/tests.rs:589 pins `ends_with("build broke\n")`.

decisions.choice: Cleanup recognition, all in checks.rs. `is_cleanup_header` keeps the three existing header forms. `is_cleanup_line` = header or content: `[command]/usr/bin/git `, `/usr/bin/git `, `Temporarily overriding HOME`, `Adding repository directory to the temporary git global config`, `Removing HTTP extra header`, `Removing includeIf`, `Complete job`, `Evaluate and set job outputs`, `##[warning]Node.js` (an optional `##[group]` prefix is ignored). `##[group]` and `##[endgroup]` alone are NOT cleanup. `failure_section` first cuts at the first header at or after the anchor, as before. Then `cleanup_start(lines, anchor)` walks back from that point (or the end) over blank lines, recognised lines, and at most `CLEANUP_GAP = 1` consecutive unrecognised lines. It stops at the anchor, at a line starting `##[group]Run ` (a step start), or at the second unrecognised line. It returns the earliest recognised line reached, and the block is cut from there. The doc comment of `is_cleanup_line` is rewritten to 'any line of CI runner cleanup text, not only the one that starts the block'.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 2 and 6. A walk from the END can only strip a trailing block, so checkout git lines at the START of a job log cannot be chosen as the cut. The `##[group]Run ` boundary (every step, including the failing `cargo xtask test-shard` step, starts with it in the raw log) separates the checkout block from the failing step even when the failing step printed 0 or 1 lines. The gap of 1 covers the real block's interleaved plain lines (`git version 2.x` between `[command]/usr/bin/git version` and the next command; `http.https://github.com/.extraheader` between two git commands). The header-first cut keeps old behaviour for logs with a header followed by unrecognised post-step text such as cache messages, so existing tests at checks.rs:857-930 and gh/tests.rs:726-772 are unchanged. Idempotence holds: after a pass, the last non-blank kept line has no recognised line within 1 unrecognised line, and the trailing note adds one more unrecognised line, so a second pass (with_failure_detail on the stored tail, CheckFailure::of) cuts nothing. A generic form such as `git version ` is not matched on its own, so a local check printing it is not touched. Input forms handled (log-line forms; no reading or admission form, so `refusal_corpus` has no case for them): header present and block after it; header absent with git/Removing/Node lines at the end; header last with the git lines above it; `##[error]` cancel line then block with no header; checkout lines at the start of the log; a single stray cleanup-looking line before the failing section (test at checks.rs:879); an all-cleanup log.

rejected.option: The previous plan's forward rule: first recognised line at or after the anchor whose suffix is at least half cleanup
rejected.why: With no marker the anchor is 0 (checks.rs:379). Checkout git lines at the start of a job log would qualify and the body would shrink to the setup lines (finding 2).
They wrap every step of a job log, so they are not specific to cleanup and would widen the cut.

rejected.option: Strip only the maximal run of recognised lines from the end, with no gap

risks.risk: A cut removes real output: a local check whose output ends in cleanup-looking lines, or a log whose real section is followed by a single recognised line.

The `##[error]` line and the progress lines stay and the block goes. (d) `failure_section_keeps_progress_after_checkout_lines_in_a_realistic_log`: `Current runner version`, `##[group]Run actions/checkout@v4`, `[command]/usr/bin/git init`, `Temporarily overriding HOME='/x' before making global git config changes`, `Adding repository directory to the temporary git global config as a safe directory`, `[command]/usr/bin/git config --global --add safe.directory /x`, `##[group]Run cargo xtask test-shard 3`, `== shard 3/6: athena-core --lib`, `running 12 tests`, `test a ... ok`, then a headerless cleanup block that repeats `Temporarily overriding HOME` and the git lines. Assert 'running 12 tests' and 'test a ... ok' survive, the checkout lines survive (`Temporarily overriding HOME` appears exactly once), and the block's `--unset-all` and `Removing HTTP extra header` lines are gone. (e) `failure_section_of_only_cleanup_says_so` (replaces the test at checks.rs:933): `cleanup_text(5)` and a git-only block return `NO_OUTPUT_NOTE` plus a newline. (f) `failure_section_of_empty_output_stays_empty`: '' and '  \n\n' come back exactly as before, and a local script `exit 3` stored via the `run_script` helper gives `output_tail == ""`.
demonstrations.observes: All `failure_section` tests pass: the new ones and the unchanged ones at checks.rs:857-930 (marker then 250 cleanup lines; a cleanup-looking line before the section is kept; no marker and no cleanup is the old tail; the jump case; wide lines). The logs without a header show no cleanup line, a realistic log keeps its progress and checkout lines, a cleanup-only log says so, and an empty log stays empty.

demonstrations.method: Every test name contains `with_failure_detail`. Literal assertions are used where the test should fail on base. (a) checks.rs `with_failure_detail_drops_headerless_cleanup_from_the_stored_tail`: `with_failure_detail` on `reused_failed("test")` (checks.rs:681) with `detail(&["athena_core x"], tail)`, where the tail is `failing units: athena-core --lib`, 5 progress lines, then the block. A passthrough closure is the redactor. Assert the units line stays first, the progress lines stay, no cleanup string is present, and a second application of `with_failure_detail` to the result changes nothing (idempotence). (b) checks.rs `with_failure_detail_and_local_run_never_store_cleanup`: `run_script` on a `sh_spec` script that prints 3 progress lines, `test demo ... FAILED`, the git removal lines, `Cleaning up orphan processes` and a Node warning, then `exit 1`. Assert the stored `output_tail` has the FAILED line and no cleanup. (c) send_back.rs, in `check_failure_tests`: `with_failure_detail_tail_is_clean_in_the_send_back`. A `CheckRun` whose `output_tail` still holds progress lines and the block goes through `CheckFailure::of` and `append_check_failures`. Assert neither the `tail` nor the brief text holds the cleanup strings. A second run whose tail ends in a note keeps the note in the brief. (d) routing.rs, in the `tests` module: `with_failure_detail_end_to_end_keeps_the_note_to_the_send_back_and_the_verifier_brief`. Build `jobs` with one cancelled shard whose log is 300 progress lines then the headerless block. Call the production `crate::gh::detail_from_job_logs(&jobs)`, put the result in a `Detailed` stub (routing.rs:565) with `Ci::new(Some(ci_run(SHA, "failure")))`, and call `run_routed_with_record(&r, SHA, &changed, &ci, &local, WAIT)` as the test at routing.rs:593 does. On the stored `test` run assert: no cleanup line; `output_tail.lines().count() <= FAILED_TAIL_LINES`; the last line starts '(no failing test section was found in'; the tail equals the detail's tail (idempotent storage). Then `crate::run::append_check_failures("brief".into(), &[crate::run::CheckFailure::of(test)])` must contain 'no failing test section was found'. Finally `crate::verify::check_result_view(test)` goes into a `VerifierInputs` built field by field like `plain_verifier_inputs` (briefs.rs:3346; all its types are pub) and `athena_context::briefs::verifier_brief(&inputs, true)` must contain the note text and no cleanup line.
demonstrations.observes: All the listed tests pass. They cover the reused-CI path (`detail_from_job_logs`, then `with_failure_detail` through `run_routed_with_record`), the local-run path (`run_check` via `run_script`), the send-back view, and the verifier brief's last-60-lines quote of a 300-line tail. On every route the cleanup lines are absent and the note is present as the last line.
